Soundbars typically come in three styles: all-in-one units (minimal setup), soundbars with subwoofers (big sound on a budget), and soundbars with subwoofers and rear speakers (real home theater audio experience) [TechRadar].
Expert testing of soundbars focuses on natural sound, where individual effects stand out from the mix, good speech clarity, immersion, and ease of use [TechRadar].
For higher-end soundbars, important features include wireless support and HDMI passthrough, including 4K 120Hz compatibility [TechRadar].

A soundbar with a mid-level rating for audio quality will sound better than a TV with a similar score [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].

Most soundbar models include multiple speakers and integrated electronics, connecting directly to a TV, and eliminating the need for a separate receiver [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Some soundbars come with a separate, typically wireless, subwoofer [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
A few soundbar models include rear speakers to offer a full surround-sound system [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Most soundbars are designed to be mounted on a wall or placed on a shelf below the TV [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Pedestal-style soundbars, known as sound bases, that a TV can sit on, have become rare due to increasing TV sizes [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Soundbars are available in a wide price range, from as little as $100 to over $1,000 [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Many highly rated soundbars typically sell for $200 to $600 [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Inexpensive soundbars often have less power and fewer features compared to separate component audio systems [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Low-priced soundbars are suitable for small or medium rooms to enhance TV sound [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Pricier, full-featured soundbars with multiple speaker arrays and powerful subwoofers can project enough sound to fill a large room [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].
Many modern soundbars function as smart speakers, offering voice control capabilities [Soundbar Buying Guide: Getting Better Audio for Your TV].

report.summary: The soundbar market in 2026 remains dominated by established brands like Samsung, Sonos, LG, and Sony, with testing data from RTINGS.com and expert reviews from TechRadar and Consumer Reports. Most highly-rated models fall in the $200–$600 range, balancing audio quality, connectivity (HDMI eARC, Dolby Atmos), and expandability. Budget options under $200 exist but sacrifice power and features; premium models ($1,000+) target cinephiles seeking full surround-sound systems.

report.summary: The 2026 soundbar landscape is led by three standout options that balance immersive multi-channel audio, Atmos capability, and convenient ecosystem features. Based on 2026 hands-on testing and expert roundups (RTINGS, PCMag Australia, CNET/WhatHiFi aggregations), Samsung HW-Q990F is the top overall pick for big rooms and dialogue clarity, Sonos Arc Ultra shines in Atmos delivery and multi-room integration, and JBL Bar 1300X offers strong performance with solid value in the premium-all-in-one category.

products.name: Samsung HW-Q990F Soundbar (11.1.4ch with Wireless Rear Speaker Kit)
pros: Best for dialogue among 2026 soundbars, delivering clear speech even in multi-channel content (RTINGS 2026).
Expansive Atmos/surround presentation with a true 11.1.4 channel array (PCMag Australia 2026 top pick).
Strong all-around performance and feature set for immersive home theater use (PCMag Australia 2026; RTINGS coverage).
cons: Very high price relative to most consumer setups (PCMag Australia 2026).
Large footprint makes it challenging to fit in small-to-medium rooms without rearranging furniture.
products.verdict: Samsung HW-Q990F remains the best overall pick for 2026 in large rooms, thanks to its class-leading dialogue clarity and 11.1.4 surround configuration; however, price and footprint are meaningful trade-offs for many buyers.
products.best_for: Large rooms, serious home theater setups, and viewers who value dialogue clarity above all

products.name: Sonos Arc Ultra Dolby Atmos Soundbar
pros: Excellent Atmos performance with a wide, cinematic soundstage (PCMag Australia 2026 list).
Best-in-class multi-room integration within the Sonos ecosystem for seamless whole-home Audio.
High build quality and intuitive app controls with frequent OTA updates.
cons: Premium price that can be hard to justify outside the Sonos ecosystem.
Relies heavily on Sonos app/eco-system; compatibility with non-Sonos devices can be less frictionless.
products.verdict: Arc Ultra stands out for Atmos and ecosystem cohesion, making it ideal for existing Sonos households; its premium price and ecosystem dependency are the main trade-offs.
products.best_for: Owners deeply invested in the Sonos ecosystem who want top-tier Atmos and easy multi-room setup

products.name: JBL Bar 1300X Soundbar
pros: Strong overall performance with multi-channel sound and solid bass for its class (PCMag Australia 2026).
Good feature set for the price, making it a compelling value among premium all-in-one bars.
Dolby Atmos capable, delivering a convincing sense of height on supported content.
cons: Not as feature-rich as flagship models (e.g., no large rear-speaker ecosystem in the base package).
May lack some versatility and future-proofing features found in the highest-end bars.
products.verdict: JBL Bar 1300X delivers strong, well-rounded performance and better value than many premium bars, but it isn’t the absolute top-of-the-line when it comes to ultimate surround experience.
products.best_for: Movie watchers in mid-to-large rooms who want impactful sound without the utmost premium price

report.summary: The 2026 soundbar market is dominated by Dolby Atmos systems with wireless subwoofers and rear speakers. Samsung's HW-Q990F leads the premium tier with an 11.1.4 configuration validated by RTINGS hands-on testing, while Sonos Arc Ultra offers the strongest all-in-one experience. Budget options like the Hisense HS2100 deliver meaningful TV-audio upgrades for around $100.

products.name: Samsung HW-Q990F
pros: 11.1.4 channel configuration with wireless subwoofer and rear speakers for genuine Dolby Atmos immersion
Named best soundbar for dialogue by RTINGS hands-on testing in March 2026
Top pick across multiple expert sources including PCMag (June 2026) and Expert Reviews (November 2025)
cons: Premium price tier — typically $1,400 and up
Large footprint requires significant space for bar, sub, and rear speakers
Samsung-specific features (Q-Symphony, SpaceFit Sound) work best with Samsung TVs
products.verdict: The Samsung HW-Q990F is the most consistently recommended premium soundbar across expert sources in 2026, with RTINGS hands-on testing naming it best for dialogue and PCMag/Expert Reviews ranking it as a top pick. Its 11.1.4 configuration with wireless subwoofer and rear speakers delivers genuine Dolby Atmos immersion for large rooms.
products.best_for: Home theater enthusiasts with large rooms who want the most immersive Dolby Atmos experience

products.name: Sonos Arc Ultra
pros: Premium all-in-one Dolby Atmos soundbar with no separate subwoofer or rears required
Top pick in PCMag's June 2026 soundbar roundup
Multi-room Sonos ecosystem integration with Era 300 surrounds and Sub for expansion
cons: Missing DTS support (noted in January 2026 hands-on comparison video)
Premium price for an all-in-one — typically around $999
Best features locked to Sonos ecosystem; limited HDMI inputs
products.verdict: The Sonos Arc Ultra is the strongest all-in-one Dolby Atmos soundbar for buyers who want premium sound without a separate subwoofer or rear speakers. PCMag ranks it as a top pick in June 2026, and it integrates seamlessly with Sonos multi-room and optional Sub/Era 300 surrounds — though DTS support is currently absent.
products.best_for: Buyers who want premium Dolby Atmos in a single bar with optional ecosystem expansion

products.name: Sonos Beam (Gen 2)
pros: Compact Dolby Atmos soundbar with HDMI eARC at a mid-range price
Named #1 budget soundbar by What HiFi in February 2026 and #1 overall by Expert Reviews in November 2025
Sonos multi-room ecosystem with optional Sub Mini and Era 100 surrounds
cons: No DTS support
Compact size limits bass impact without adding a Sub Mini
Premium price for the size class — typically around $449
products.verdict: The Sonos Beam Gen 2 remains the best mid-range compact Dolby Atmos soundbar in 2026, recommended as #1 budget pick by What HiFi (February 2026) and #1 overall by Expert Reviews (November 2025). It delivers genuine Atmos from a small footprint and integrates with the Sonos ecosystem for expansion.
products.best_for: Mid-range buyers who want compact Dolby Atmos with ecosystem expansion options

products.name: JBL Bar 1000MK2
pros: Detachable wireless rear speakers for true surround without permanent installation
